hints.title: Sorting Limit and Linear Scan Obstacle
hints.text: Sorting the numbers allows a linear scan to find consecutive runs, but takes O(N log N) time. How can you determine if a number is the true beginning of a streak without inspecting every other element first?

hints.title: Sequence Start Condition
hints.text: A number x can only start a consecutive sequence if x - 1 does not exist in the collection. Only counting streaks from verified sequence starters ensures each number is visited at most twice.

hints.title: Hash Set Lookup and Streak Counting
hints.text: Insert all numbers into a set for fast lookup. Iterate through the set; if num - 1 is not in the set, num is the start of a streak. Incrementally check for num + 1, num + 2, and so on, updating the maximum length found.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

variables: N: length of nums array (0 <= N <= 10^5)
complexity.notes: Each element is checked as a sequence starter at most once, and visited at most once during streak expansion, yielding 2N lookups total.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Sorting the array achieves O(N log N) time, which violates the strict O(N) runtime complexity requirement specified in the problem prompt.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Using O(N) auxiliary memory to store elements in a hash set achieves strict O(N) linear runtime.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Identification of the sequence-start condition (num - 1 not in set) to prevent O(N^2) worst-case traversal, handling empty input, duplicate numbers, and negative values.

solutions.approach: Hash Set with Sequence Starter Verification
